'''Edward Meredith Burgess''' (June 8, 1934 – June 24, 2018) was an American [[chemist]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Obituary: Edward M. Burgess |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-Edward-M-Burgess/96/i41 |publisher=C & en |access-date=6 October 2021}}</ref> He specialized in [[organic chemistry]] with an emphasis on [[chemical synthesis|methodology]], [[chemical structure|structure]], and [[photochemistry]]. He is best known for the [[Burgess reagent]] (methyl ''N''-(triethylammoniumsulfonyl)carbamate) that is used for selective dehydration of alcohols.<ref name=EMB_01>{{cite journal | title = The reactions of an ''N''-sulfonylamine inner salt |author1=Atkins, G. M. |author2=Burgess, E. M. | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | year = 1968 | volume = 90 |issue=17 | pages = 4744–4745 | doi = 10.1021/ja01019a052|bibcode=1968JAChS..90.4744A }}</ref><ref name=EMB_O2>{{cite journal | title = Thermal reactions of alkyl ''N''-carbomethoxysulfamate esters |author1=Edward M. Burgess |author2=Harold R. Penton Jr. |author3=E. A. Taylor | journal = [[J. Org. Chem.]] | year = 1973 | volume = 38 | issue = 1 | pages = 26–31 | doi = 10.1021/jo00941a006}}</ref>

Professor Burgess served as Secretary-Treasurer of the Organic Division of the [[American Chemical Society]] from 1974 to 1977.<ref name=EMB_03>[http://www.organicdivision.org/?nd=archives_history  ACS Organic Division Archive.] - Retrieved 2010-12-28.</ref>

==Biography==
Edward Meredith Burgess was born in [[Birmingham, Alabama|Birmingham]], [[Alabama]] in 1934. He attended [[Shades Valley High School]] in that city and was awarded the school's science award upon graduation in 1951. During the summers of his junior and senior high school years he obtained a job performing routine chores at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]] (UAB) Department of [[Biochemistry]]. It was during this period at UAB that Burgess began his career in [[chemistry|chemical]] [[research]]. Under the guidance of the noted [[carbohydrate]] [[chemist]], [[William Ward Pigman]], he was given his own research project, the “''Anhydrous Reaction of [[Nitrogen Dioxide]] with some Selected [[Sugars]].''”

In 1952, Burgess was awarded an [[NROTC]] [[scholarship]] and entered [[Auburn University]] with a dual major in [[chemistry]] and [[physics]]. During his [[undergraduate]] years at [[Auburn University|Auburn]] he undertook research in the laboratories of Frank Stevens (Chemistry) on the Synthesis of [[Indole]] Derivatives useful as [[Plant growth regulator|Plant Growth Regulators]] and Howard Carr (Physics) on the construction of a [[mass spectrometer]]. He obtained his B.Sc. degree ([[cum laude]]) in 1956.

From 1956 to 1959, Burgess served as an officer aboard the [[United States Navy|US Navy]] [[destroyer]], [[USS Stormes|USS ''Stormes'' (DD-780)]], a ship assigned to both the [[U.S. Atlantic Fleet|U.S. Atlantic]] and [[United States Sixth Fleet|Mediterranean fleets]].

==Research==
===Graduate research===
As a graduate student in the [[George Büchi|Büchi]] group at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Burgess's research focused largely on [[Synthetic organic chemistry#Organic synthesis|synthetic organic chemistry]] and [[photochemistry]]. His doctoral [[dissertation]] was titled “Photochemical isomerization of eucarvone and cyclooctatrienone; Studies toward the synthesis of [[samandarin]].”<ref name=EMB_Dissertation>Edward M. Burgess (1962), ''Photochemical isomerization of eucarvone and cyclooctatrienone; Studies toward the synthesis of samandarin.'' Ph.D. Thesis, Massachusetts Institute of Technology. [http://library.mit.edu/item/000744472 Online catalog entry]. Retrieved 2011-01-27.</ref> An interest in [[photochemistry]] and [[Synthetic organic chemistry#Organic synthesis|synthetic methodology]] would mark many of Burgess's contributions to chemistry. In addition to his publications with Professor Büchi connected with his dissertation,<ref name=EMB_04>{{cite journal |author1=G. Büchi |author2=E. M. Burgess | title = Photochemical reactions. IX. Isomerization of eucarvone. | year = 1960 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 82 | issue = 16 | pages = 4333–4337 | doi = 10.1021/ja01501a052|bibcode=1960JAChS..82.4333B }}</ref><ref name=EMB_05>{{cite journal |author1=G. Büchi |author2=E. M. Burgess | title = Photochemical reactions. X. Experiments with 1,3,5-cyclooctatrien-7-one, and cyclooctatetraene epoxide. | year = 1962 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 84 | issue = 16 | pages = 3104–3109 | doi = 10.1021/ja00875a014|bibcode=1962JAChS..84.3104B }}</ref> Burgess also published independently on the epoxidation of cholestadienone.<ref name=EMB_06>{{cite journal | author = E. M. Burgess | title = 4,5β-Epoxycholest-1-en-3-one. | year = 1962 | journal = [[J. Org. Chem.]] | volume = 27 | issue = 4 | pages = 1433–1434 | doi = 10.1021/jo01051a501}}</ref><br>
